title: High-Altitude Platform System (HAPS) for Ultra-Long-Range (ULR) Wireless Backhaul
description: ***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.*** This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/high-altitude-platform-system-ultra-long-range-wireless-backhaul The Department of National Defence (DND), Shared Services Canada (SSC) and National Research Council of Canada (NRC) are seeking the development of a solution that will extend the reach of ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e. over-the-horizon ranges) using High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS). Challenge sponsor: National Research Council (NRC) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date : October 20, 2026 Closing date : December 1, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Problem statement The Government of Canada recognizes the critical role that advanced communication technologies play in supporting national defence, public safety, and the security of Canadians. Reliable and resilient connectivity in dangerous, remote, and sparsely populated regions is essential for effective defence operations, emergency response, and border monitoring. However, delivering such connectivity remains a significant challenge due to Canada’s vast geography, low population densities, and extreme environmental conditions. The Department of National Defence, Shared Services Canada and National Research Council of Canada are seeking the development of a solution that leverages High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) to provide ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e., over-the-horizon ranges). This capability will enhance communications under harsh weather or challenging terrain in theatres of conflict, in remote areas, and isolated regions with little to no current connectivity. The ultimate goal is to improve secure, high-speed communications for Canadian defence, surveillance, and emergency operations while also potentially benefiting civilian emergency response connectivity needs. The successful applicant is responsible for securing a demonstration site as well as a Special Flight Operations Certificate (SFOC) clearance from Transport Canada to demonstrate the HAPS capabilities. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Demonstrate the capability to travel from the surface up to 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers and travel laterally within the corridor of 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers. 2. Operate at a specified, nominal, fixed point relative to the Earth for an extended period (minimum of 3 days). 3. Launch, deploy, and operate from land or water-based environments. 4. Provide a minimum of 100 Watts to support the deployment of long-range sensors. 5. Deliver high-bandwidth, high-availability, ultra-low latency wireless connectivity comparable to current offerings (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) in the telecommunications industry. 6. Support current (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) wireless systems and infrastructure. 7. Provide a minimum of 1000 km² service area coverage and a minimum of 200 km² of transit area coverage based on usage demands. 8. Be deployable within 6 hours for heavier-than-air HAPS or within 24 hours for lighter-than-air HAPS. 9. Incorporate automated decision-making for flight maneuvers and operations. 10. Operate at cold temperatures between -50 to at least -70 degrees Celsius. Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Have a power management system that optimizes power consumption and adapts to usage demand. 2. Be capable of continuous power generation and recharging during ground operations and flight through renewable energy sources. 3. Have non-assisted launch and land capability from land or water-based environments. 4. Support next generation wireless systems and infrastructure. 5. Maintain wireless connectivity in the presence of intentional and unintentional wireless channel interference. 6. Provide communications link security features and platform hardening to prevent signal interception, hacking and unauthorized platform hijacking. 7. Demonstrate the ability to daisy chain the signal using intra-HAPS (i.e HAPS group 1 to HAPS group2), and/or inter-HAPS (between individual HAPS). 8. Support backhauling requirements for future wireless networks. 9. Complement the terrestrial communication infrastructures. 10. Minimize the amount of traditional backhaul hopping. 11. Support point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, and mesh links. Background and context High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) are unmanned vehicles designed to operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 20 to 50 kilometers above the Earth's surface. HAPS are classified into two main types: Lighter-than-air (LTA) platforms and Heavier-than-air (HTA) platforms. LTA platforms include balloons and airships characterized by low energy consumption but has limited maneuverability. On the other hand, HTA platforms which include light unmanned aircrafts that rely on electric motors to generate and maintain lift offer greater maneuverability but have payload weight restrictions and can have an energy deficit issue as a result of prolonged dark periods during winter months at higher latitudes. HAPS offer several advantages such as its ability to be airborne for long durations and less expensive to operate compared to satellites. Since HAPS fly at lower altitudes than satellites, they are able to provide low latency data communications. The propulsion systems for HAPS generally use sustainable energy sources which have a lower environmental impact than rocket launches for satellites. Presently, existing wireless backhaul technologies have limitations in terms of coverage and during emergency situations for remote areas, nomadic users, and scattered populations. A merging solution between HAPS and ULR (Ultra-Long-Range) wireless backhaul, offering broadband services, would be a great benefit to a wide range of populations, especially in times of crisis and during emergency situations where traditional telecommunication services suffer outages. Additionally, HAPS are highly effective platforms for enhancing military communications and remote sensing capabilities. They can be used to complement military satcom infrastructure, offering capabilities in intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. When equipped with high-resolution cameras, radars, and signals intelligence systems (SIGINT), HAPS provide continuous coverage of areas of interest. title: Jurisdictional Scan and Case Studies for Seabed Licensing Regime
description: The primary objective of this work is to develop four case studies examining how other jurisdictions have designed and implemented their respective seabed licencing frameworks for subsea transmission cables and corridors, with an emphasis on frameworks dealing with subsea cables that connect offshore wind projects to onshore electrical infrastructure. Using the four selected case studies, the contractor will develop and recommend options for the seabed licencing framework for subsea transmission cables and corridors within the jointly managed Canada-Nova Scotia offshore area.

title: Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the items detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2. The Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 is required as a specialized explosive charge used by combat engineers to breach barbed wire obstacles/entanglements and to clear a path through anti-personnel mines, without requiring personnel to approach the obstacle directly under fire. The system consists of several cylindrical sections of tubes/pipes that can be connected end-to end to create a linear explosive charge of desired length. A blunt, rounded nose sleeve is attached to the leading end of the assembly, allowing the torpedo to be pushed or shoved through obstacles, such as concertina wire or across rough terrain, without snagging. The Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 is primed with a blasting cap. When detonated, the pipe itself contributes to the effect: the metal casing fractures into high-velocity fragments that shred the surrounding wire, while the explosive blast clears a path for infantry to advance. title: Kouvolan kaupungin pienet purkutyöt v.2027
description: Kouvolan kaupungin pienet purkutyöt v.2027 Kouvolan kaupunki hakee puitesopimuskumppaneita kaupungin pienille purkutöille vuodelle 2027. Toimeksiannot ovat Kouvolan kaupungin pienien rakennusten purkutöitä. Purkutyön toimeksianto voi sisältää myös alihankintaa, esim. asbestipurkutyöt. Toimeksiantojen kohteet sijaitsevat Kouvolan alueella. Tyypillisimpiä kohteita ovat puurakenteiset omakotitalot perustuksineen. Purkutoimeksiantoon tavallisesti kuuluu rakennukseen liittyvien LVIS-tele-järjestelmien purkaminen kiinteistöstä, kaivaminen ja tulppaaminen tilaajan esittämiin kohtiin sekä purkualueen tasaus. Puitesopimuksessa sekä toimeksiannossa noudetaan YSE 1998 sopimusehtoja ellei tarjouspyynnössä tai sopimuksessa toisin mainittu. Puitesopimusjärjestelyyn pääsevät mukaan kaikki tarjouspyynnön soveltuvuusvaatimukset, kelpoisuusehdot ja hankinnan kohteen kriteerit täyttävät tarjoajat. Sopimuskautena ei sitouduta mihinkään hankintamääriin. Toimeksiantojen antaminen liitteenä olevan sopimusluonnoksen mukaisesti. Ennen työn aloittamista urakoitsija antaa kirjallisen arvion kohteen urakkakustannuksista. Työn toteuttamisen ajankohta ja valmistuminen sovitaan ennen työn aloittamista. Lähtökohtaisesti tämän kilpailutuksen puitesopimuksia käyttää Kouvolan Tilapalvelut sekä Tekniikan ja ympäristön toimiala, mutta myös muut kaupungin yksiköt voivat hyödyntää puitesopimuksia. Lisäksi puitejärjestelyyn kuuluu osallistuminen purkutyöhön liittyvään kehitystyöhön. Tilaajan tavoitteena on kehittää purkutyön tilausta ja suoritusta tukemaan enemmän kiertotalouden tavoitteiden saavuttamista. Kehitystyön sisällöstä ja kustannuksista sovitaan erikseen toimeksiantokohtaisesti ja ne voivat sisältyä yksittäiseen purkutyön toimeksiantoon.,

title: FCI Leavenworth Cable Television Services
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution Leavenworth, requests quotations for cable television services from eligible vendors. Quotation Requirements: Vendors shall submit: � A proposed channel lineup identifying how it meets the SOW requirements and clearly identifying any substitutions or exceptions. � A brief technical approach explaining how service will be provided to approximately 115 television drops at the FCI and FPC using the existing distribution system. Identify any equipment, installation, or modifications required and describe responsibility for equipment maintenance and repairs. � A transition approach identifying the time required to activate service and measures to minimize service interruptions. � A description of telephone support, outage assessment, on-site response, and service restoration capabilities. � References for up to three recent, relevant contracts involving comparable television distribution services. Vendors without relevant past performance shall state that in their quotation. � Separate pricing for the base period and each of the four option periods, including recurring service, installation, equipment, preventive maintenance, and any other charges necessary to perform the SOW. Identify any exceptions to the requested terms. Comparative Evaluation: The Government will use a comparative evaluation to determine which quotation provides the best value. Quotations will be compared directly against one another using technical capability, past performance, and price. Numerical scores will not be assigned. Technical capability will consider the proposed channel lineup, compatibility with the existing distribution system, installation and transition approach, and ability to meet maintenance and outage-response requirements. Past performance will consider available information regarding successful performance of similar services, including reliability, responsiveness, and customer satisfaction. A vendor without relevant past performance will receive a neutral assessment under this factor. Technical capability and past performance, when combined, are more important than price. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its documented benefits justify the additional price. Total evaluated price will include the base period, all four option periods, and all required charges. Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise them. Select Best-Suited, Then Negotiate: The Government intends to select the best-suited vendor based on the initial quotations but reserves the right to conduct exchanges. After identifying the apparent best-suited vendor, the Government may negotiate price, technical details, transition arrangements, or other terms with that vendor to finalize the requirement and obtain the best value. Identification as the apparent best-suited vendor does not constitute an award. If the parties cannot reach an acceptable agreement, the Government may end negotiations and engage the next best-suited vendor based on the evaluation. Vendors should submit their best initial quotations because the Government may make award without exchanges. Quotations must include: legal business name, business address, UEI, a point of contact, telelphone number, and e-mail address. All quotations must be submitted by e-mail to FCI Leavenworth Contract Specialist Kathleen Wood at kwood1@bop.gov.

description: IT Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) Managed Services Request for Information VA-27-00019920 Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512 with a size standard of $34 million. VA seeks market research on industry capability to meet the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), the feasibility of key requirements, barriers to competition, and recommended changes. Responses should address the specific PWS requirements rather than provide generic marketing or capability statements. Cite relevant PWS paragraph numbers and clearly mark proprietary information. For each numbered question, indicate whether the principal requirements are (a) achievable as written, (b) achievable with modifications, or (c) not currently achievable; explain material limitations and recommend specific changes. Respondents may propose functionally equivalent, technology-neutral solutions. Responses shall be limited to 20 pages, excluding the cover/firm information, comparable-experience summary, and ROM attachment. Respondents shall indicate its company name and address; point of contact, phone, and email; business size and socioeconomic status; applicable NAICS code(s); Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); and available contract vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC). VOSB/SDVOSB respondents should provide proof of SBA certification. Separately provide a concise summary of comparable contracts (agency, contract number, approximate value, and reference contact, if available). Additionally, VOSB/SDVOSB respondents shall indicate your company s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in accordance with VAAR 852.219-73 (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION) VA Notice of Total Set-Aside For Certified SDVOSBs and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database (excluding direct costs to the extent they are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and the SDVOSB/VOSB does not provide the service, such as airline travel, cloud computing services, or mass media purchases). When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the service portion of the contract. Your response shall include information as to available personnel and financial resources; full names of proposed team members and the PWS requirements planned to be subcontracted to them, which must include the prime planned percentage or the names of the potential team members that may be used to fulfill the set aside requirement. Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PWS and must address the following: 1. Transition-In and Service Continuity (PWS 5.2 and 5.4.6) The draft PWS provides two concurrent transition tracks: Track A for platform/CCI services (approximately Day 60 operational transfer when retaining the current platform or Day 150 for a different platform) and Track B for Tier 0/Tier 1 services (100% workload at required service levels within 150 calendar days), with Quality Gates and 30 days of hypercare after each transfer. Can your company meet these timelines while maintaining uninterrupted functionality and customer experience? Identify the most consequential dependencies, transition risks, baseline verification and operational transfer readiness criteria, and any alternative sequencing or technology approaches that would reduce risk. How should VA address capabilities discovered after award that are absent from the Functional Baseline (Attachment 2)? Identify only authorization, integration, or other deliverable deadlines that materially affect feasibility. 2. Managed Services Delivery Model and Tier 0/Tier 1 Operations (PWS 3.0, 4.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5.5, and 5.6) Can your company deliver the integrated Tier 0/Tier 1 service desk, CCI, knowledge management, process integration, quality assurance, and performance reporting requirements through a single managed service, with results independently verified for VA? Identify capability gaps, specialized teaming needs, or requirements that could unnecessarily restrict competition. Comment on feasibility of the draft workload assumptions, including approximately 2,700 knowledge articles (15% annual growth), 520 instructional videos annually, approximately 35 concurrent process-integration initiatives (10% annual growth), Top 10 user support, and Enterprise Command Center support via Tier 1 Incident Management Analysts. What changes or technology-neutral approaches would improve delivery without reducing required outcomes? 3. Artificial Intelligence and Automation Capabilities (PWS 5.8) Can your company implement and operate the AI and automation capabilities described in the PWS, including conversational, generative and agentic AI, robotic process automation, self-service, agent-assist knowledge surfacing, and post-interaction summaries? Distinguish commercially available capabilities from those requiring configuration, integration, or custom development; identify security, data, quality assurance, and operational dependencies. Describe how inaccurate AI-generated content would be detected and corrected before entry into permanent records. Recommend additional capabilities that could materially improve resolution, accessibility, customer experience, or agent productivity, distinguishing demonstrated solutions from emerging functionality. 4. Automation Glide Path Feasibility and Governance (PWS 5.8.3 5.8.5, 5.8.10, 5.8.11, 5.8.14, and 6.1.12) The draft PWS proposes human-handled capacity of 92%, 82%, 72%, 65%, and 60% of a certified baseline in Years 1 5 (50% floor), using approximately 126,000 monthly contacts as the current planning baseline. Are these targets achievable while sustaining service quality? Recommend changes to baseline certification, timing, assumptions, exclusions, and measurement, including the definition of an Automated Resolution (no agent and no repeat contact within seven days), treatment of pre-existing automation, and human-handled contacts per 1,000 End Users. Address how AI-attempted contacts escalated to agents should be counted and reported. Are the proposed approval controls practical (intent-level parity baseline of approximately 90 days, Automation Deployment Package, approximately 15-business-day VA review, and rollback within approximately 15 minutes for voice/chat or four hours for other channels)? Recommend changes that balance deployment speed, auditability, accessible escalation, and protection against unsuccessful deflection. Include any potential price and service level impacts associated with the glide path iterative drops in human-handled capacity. 5. Staffing, Workforce Management, and Surge Capacity (PWS 4.2, 5.1.4, 5.3, and 5.8.7) Can your company meet 24/7/365 support from continental U.S. facilities, the required service levels, and the proposed peak-day planning assumption

title: Atviras projekto konkursas "Utenos miesto daugiafunkcinio sporto komplekso rekonstravimas"
description: Konkurso tikslas: išrinkti geriausiai urbanistinius, architektūros ir funkcinius aspektus bei kitus reikalavimus (išvardintus šiose konkurso sąlygose, užduotyje „Utenos miesto daugiafunkcinio sporto komplekso rekonstravimas“, atitinkančią projekto architektūrinę idėją. Šio konkurso I-ą, II-ą ir III-ą vietas užėmusių projekto pasiūlymų autoriams bus skiriamos piniginės išmokos: I-ai vietai skiriama 6.000 Eur, II-ai – 4.000 Eur, III-iai – 3.000 Eur. Šis pirkimas vykdomas, nenumatant sudaryti pirkimo sutarties. Perkančioji organizacija, vadovaudamasi Viešųjų pirkimų įstatymo 71 straipsnio 4 dalies nuostatomis, numato vykdyti atskirą paslaugų pirkimą dėl „Utenos miesto daugiafunkcinio sporto komplekso rekonstravimas“ (projektinių pasiūlymų, techninio darbo projekto, statybą leidžiančio dokumento gavimo, darbo projekto ar jo dalių parengimo bei statinio projekto vykdymo priežiūros paslaugos), į jas kviečiant I vietą užėmusio projekto pasiūlymo dalyvį (Pastaba: Šio konkurso laimėtoju yra laikomas I vietą užėmusio projekto pasiūlymo dalyvis). Projektinių pasiūlymų, techninio darbo projekto, statybą leidžiančio dokumento gavimo bei statinio projekto vykdymo priežiūros paslaugų kaina neturi viršyti 181.500,00 Eur su PVM, jei tiekėjas yra PVM mokėtojas, arba 150.000,00 Eur be PVM, jei tiekėjas nėra PVM mokėtojas.

Applicants who require a personnel security clearance are responsible for all costs associated with fingerprinting. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at Jasper National Park Train Station at 607 Connaught Drive, Jasper, AB on November 12. The site visit will begin at 1PM ABT, at the Parks Canada Front Desk Area. Bidders must communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than November 11 to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders must also complete and submit a certification. Bidders who do not confirm attendance, provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend, or who do not complete and submit the above certification as required will not be allowed access to the site. Bidders will be required to sign an attendance sheet. Bidders should confirm in their bid that they have attended the site visit. Bidders who do not attend the mandatory site visit or do not send a representative will not be given an alternative appointment and their bid will be declared non-responsive. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. title: J012--Fire Suppression System Maintenance and Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning
description: Fire Suppression System Maintenance and Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Richard L Roudebush VA Medical Center 1481 West 10th Street, Indianapolis, Indiana 46202 Additional service location: 9045 East 59th Street, Building 402, Indianapolis, Indiana 46216 The Contractor shall maintain the identified fire suppression systems in a serviceable condition, remove grease accumulation from the complete identified kitchen exhaust systems, and maintain the Building 402 grease trap. The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, transportation, tools, access equipment, routine maintenance materials, cleaning supplies, waste handling, testing, service labels, and documentation required by this PWS. The recurring scope includes five kitchen fire suppression systems and five Kidde IND-21 Hazmat dry chemical systems, with monthly inspections of all ten systems, semiannual maintenance and service certification, and annual maintenance tasks. All five hoods require quarterly exhaust inspections and complete interior and exterior cleaning. The Building 402 grease trap requires quarterly inspection, pump-out, and cleaning. Appendix A identifies equipment and locations; Appendix B states service quantities, deliverables, and performance standards. The prime Contractor remains responsible for all subcontracted work and for submitting complete records directly to the COR. A kitchen cleaning report does not document fire suppression system maintenance, monthly suppression inspections, or grease-trap service; each service shall have its own identifiable record.

The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek esolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to llow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: Fire Suppression System Maintenance and Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Richard L Roudebush VA Medical Center 1481 West 10th Street, Indianapolis, Indiana 46202 Additional service location: 9045 East 59th Street, Building 402, Indianapolis, Indiana 46216 The Contractor shall maintain the identified fire suppression systems in a serviceable condition, remove grease accumulation from the complete identified kitchen exhaust systems, and maintain the Building 402 grease trap. A kitchen cleaning report does not document fire suppression system maintenance, monthly suppression inspections, or grease-trap service; each service shall have its own identifiable record.

title: Urgent - Independent Medical Expert Advisory Opinion | Neurosurgery or Orthopedic Surgery
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), is seeking capable and qualified recognized medical schools, universities, clinics, and medical institutions to provide independent medical expert advisory opinion described in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Government intends to negotiate a sole source acquisition using the expert services authority in Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-3(b)(3), which permits other than full and open competition, when its conditions are met, to acquire the services of an expert or neutral person for current or anticipated litigation or dispute. The required advisory opinion relates to a disputed VA benefits claim, the Board of Veterans' Appeals remand, and related judicial proceedings. The specified service sought is an independent physician expert opinion, not mediation or other alternative dispute resolution services. Issuance of this Sources Sought does not guarantee award. The Government will not reimburse offer preparation costs, and offerors should clearly mark proprietary or sensitive information. Interested vendors able to meet the requirement of the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS), Independent Medical Expert Advisory Opinion - Neurosurgery or Orthopedic Surgery, are requested to submit a written technical capability statement. The technical capability statement should address the following: � The recognized medical school, university, clinic, or medical institution that would furnish the independent advisory opinion and the nature of the proposed arrangement. � How an appropriate institutional official will select a physician with neurosurgery or orthopedic-surgery expertise; verify credentials and independence; and ensure the ordinary VA compensation and pension examination/opinion vendor channel is not used. � Capacity to receive, protect, and review a substantial longitudinal medical record through an approved secure process, including any strictly administrative intermediary and restrictions on its role. � Ability to provide a complete, reasoned, signed advisory opinion; acknowledge receipt within two business days; meet the 30-day requested delivery and anticipated 45-day period of performance; and identify any constraints or dependencies. Interested vendors must provide a designated point of contact, proof of SAM.gov registration, address the expert qualifications, institutional selection and independence, secure records handling, and other requirements of the attached PWS. Interested vendors are encouraged to include a firm-fixed price quote with their capability statements for meeting the requirements in the attached PWS. The VA may request clarifications; or seek negotiations on a sole source basis in accordance with RFO reference above. Interested vendors should provide their submissions by Tuesday, December 1, 2026, no later than 10:00 AM ET via email to Brian.Kadel@va.gov and MDECONTRACTING@va.gov. Please limit submissions to five pages, excluding the cover sheet and index.

title: Weapons Effect Solicitation
description: This solicitation is related to Notice IDs: N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014 and N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014_Rev1. The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea and surface vessels to develop and utilize specialized software codes that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire events and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of computational models; 5) Solve finite element models elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. title: Anzio Industry Day
description: The Anzio program aims to develop innovative aero-assist technologies for spacecraft, which will enable large, rapid, and precise orbit transfers while significantly reducing propellant requirements. In support of this goal, technology areas of interest to DARPA for execution of this program include thermal protection systems, control systems and algorithms, atmospheric sensing, and lightweight aeroshells. Technology areas that are not of interest include communications, power management, spacecraft buses, payloads, propulsion systems, and existing orbital transfer vehicles.

title: J065--Karl Storz Laryngoscope Protection1 Comprehensive Service at Edward Hines Jr. VA Hospital
description: Under Statutory Authority 41 U.S.C. 1901 the Great Lakes Acquisition Center (GLAC) intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Karl Storz Endoscopy-America, Inc for Protection1 Comprehensive Service (Repair and Exchanges) for the Karl Storz Laryngoscopes. Karl Storz is the only vendor authorized to provide repairs and exchanges of these laryngoscopes. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. The Protection1 Comprehensive Service is already in use. This request is for sustainment of an existing service. This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 1901 Simplified acquisition procedures as implemented in RFO 12.102, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This will be a firm fixed price contract for a one-year base plus four (4) one-year options. The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) is 811210 with a business size standard of $34.0 Million. No solicitation documents are available and telephone requests will not be accepted. However, any firm that believes it can meet these requirements may give written notification to the Contracting Officer by 10:00 AM Local Time (Central) Tuesday, December 1, 2026. Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to comply with the above requirements. This evidence shall include a letter from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) stating vendor is an authorized service vendor per VAAR Clause 852.212-71(c). Information must be sent to the Contracting Officer, Joni Dorr, joni.dorr@va.gov. Responses received will be evaluated, however a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.
